task.description: WF-03 Step 2 (design) for ISS-0428: design adopting scripts/test_parallel.sh inside mix letflow.check.test (the actual gate CI/every WF-02/WF-03 run is blocked on), which currently still shells to plain `mix test`. Must settle: (1) the ISS-0069 warning-substring gate, currently pointed at one captured subprocess stream, must be re-pointed at the N per-partition logs test_parallel.sh writes instead of the aggregated stdout it prints -- and the design must specify how the implementation proves it still catches a real occurrence, not just assert it will. (2) whether the two other isolated subprocess runs (--only wasm_hang, --only lua_wallclock_race) stay serial or change, argued not asserted. (3) selection mechanism -- selectable-per-host vs. wholesale switch, decided honestly against this session's own fresh measurement (N=2, CI's real parallelism, now measured at 1.89x and clean -- superseding the issue's own filed pessimism that N=16's 2.9x wouldn't transfer to a 2-vCPU runner). (4) failure-mode parity -- a failing parallel run must still tell an agent which test failed and why without them having to find a discarded CI tmp dir. (5) explicit scope boundary against ISS-0423 (async:true/parallelism-within-partition, a separate open issue). Design doc only, no implementation code, no edits to mix.exs/letflow.check.test.ex/scripts/ci.yml themselves.

result.summary:
Design written to lib/letflow/design/iss0428-parallel-runner-in-check-test.md. No .ex/.exs code blocks anywhere in the file (verified: zero ``` fences, zero defmodule/def/defp occurrences) -- signatures and contracts only, per role file's Forbidden section.

DECISION ON ITEM 1 (ISS-0069 gate): re-point at the N per-partition logs, not test_parallel.sh's aggregated stdout. Mechanism specified in design section 1.2: parse the runner's own already-existing 'test_parallel: partition logs in <dir>' stdout line (confirmed present unconditionally in scripts/test_parallel.sh by reading it) to discover the mktemp'd log directory, glob partition-*.log under it (no hardcoded N), concatenate their content, and apply the exact same two checks run/1 applies today (nonzero exit -> raise; substring present -> raise with offending lines, now partition-attributed). Both 'line not found' and 'zero partition logs found' are hard Mix.raise failures, never a silent pass-through -- this is the section's central point, since silently passing on either miss would recreate the exact vacuous-gate hazard the issue names. PROOF OBLIGATION specified in section 1.3: a scratch (never-committed) probe that injects a real ISS-0069-shaped unused-default-argument helper into an already-compiled test-support file, runs the re-pointed check against it (must fail, must name the offending partition log), then reverts and confirms clean. Both runs' real output must be quoted per No Speculation -- this is assigned to ELIXIR-DEV at implementation and re-verified by TEST-RUNNER, not something this design step could run itself since it requires editing check.test.ex which is forbidden here.

DECISION ON ITEM 2: both isolated subprocess runs (wasm_hang, lua_wallclock_race) stay serial and structurally unchanged. Argued explicitly in section 2, not merely asserted: both exist BECAUSE OF contention sensitivity (wasm_hang leaks into a shared node-global native worker pool per ISS-0352's own moduledoc; lua_wallclock_race needs freedom from wall-clock contention per ISS-0426, and ISS-0423's own discovered_side_effect already recorded that 6-way parallel running is what surfaced that flake). Parallelizing either would multiply or reintroduce the exact hazard each was isolated to escape, and neither is large enough for the parallel-runner's throughput motivation to apply. Flagged as revisitable only with its own future measurement, not decided here.

DECISION ON ITEM 3 (the one you asked me to report specifically): SWITCH WHOLESALE, no selector flag, no host-detection branch, no silent fallback to plain `mix test`. This directly reverses ISS-0428's own suggested shape (selectable, CI stays on serial 'until measured') because the thing that suggestion was hedging against -- CI's N=2 gain being unproven and plausibly negative -- is now closed by this session's own measurement: 1.89x, clean, no connection exhaustion, no crashes, at N=2 specifically (CI's real ubuntu-latest parallelism). Argued in section 3: keeping a selector after the uncertainty it existed for is gone is unjustified complexity -- two code paths through check.test's main-suite step is two things that can independently drift, and CI (the path that matters most) would get the least exercise of whichever branch isn't the default. No mix.exs or ci.yml edit is needed for CI to pick this up: REQ-136's own design note (ci.yml's own comment block) already establishes CI runs exactly one `mix letflow.check` step, so changing what check.test does internally changes CI behavior automatically, confirming ISS-0423's own test_parallel_adoption_point note. N-derivation itself is untouched -- test_parallel.sh's own nproc/getconf/TEST_PARALLEL_N logic, unmodified, naturally yields N=2 on ubuntu-latest with no new CI env var.

The genuinely distinct hazard the dispatch asked about (bash-less/no-nproc hosts, since this project runs on both Windows and Linux) is answered separately in section 3.1: this session's own host IS Windows (MINGW64/Git Bash) and test_parallel.sh already ran successfully on it all session -- 'Windows' alone is not disqualifying, 'no POSIX shell at all' is, and no host in this project's actual fleet (this workstation, CI's ubuntu-latest) lacks bash. Design requires run_main_suite/0 to resolve `bash` via System.find_executable/1 (matching the module's own existing pattern) and Mix.raise loudly, immediately, with no silent fallback, if bash is absent -- explicitly argued as a considered position (a broken-toolchain host should fail loud, not quietly run a different, less-tested code path) and flagged in section 3.1's own text as open for REVIEWER/CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR to contest if they disagree, since the case being guarded against is hypothetical/unobserved rather than measured.

ITEM 4 (failure-mode parity): section 4 requires run_main_suite/0 to print full content of every partition log showing a real Failed: line or a missing Result: line (crash) BEFORE raising, re-using the same log-directory discovery from item 1's check (one discovery, two consumers) -- so a failing run's terminal/CI-log output contains actual per-test failure detail, not just aggregate counts, and the Mix.raise message itself names the log directory path for durability. Explicitly does not add a ci.yml artifact-upload step (out of this doc's declared scope) -- reasoned that CI already retains full job-log output regardless of the underlying mktemp dir's lifetime, so printing to stdout is sufficient; artifact upload is flagged as a candidate follow-up issue in the open questions, not decided here.

ITEM 5 (ISS-0423 boundary): section 5 states it explicitly -- ISS-0423 covers async:true-capability WITHIN a partition/BEAM (test/support/tenant_fixture.ex's global Sandbox.mode(:auto) call defeating async, tied to ISS-0113); this design covers only WHICH SUBPROCESS check.test shells out to and how its own gates adapt to a multi-log shape. The two compose without further change -- a future async-capable partition just finishes faster, unaffected by this design's log-discovery/substring-check mechanics.

Open questions listed explicitly in section 8, not silently resolved: whether the ISS-0069 probe becomes a permanent regression test (left to TEST-DESIGNER); whether wasmex's worker pool is genuinely OS-process-scoped (unresolved, matters only if wasm_hang parallelism is reconsidered later); whether CI should additionally upload the partition-log directory as a build artifact (flagged as a candidate follow-up, out of this doc's own declared scope); whether bash-resolution should try a WSL fallback if plain bash is absent (not designed, unobserved need).

Did not run mix compile/mix test as part of this step since no lib/ file was touched (design-doc-only step, matching the role file's own scope) -- the design itself was cross-checked against directly-read source (letflow.check.test.ex read in full, scripts/test_parallel.sh read in full, decision 0009 read in full, ci.yml read in full) rather than assumed.
